QuestionStmt.S: In a bank, the principal increases continuously at a rate of $x\%$ per year. Then the rate $x$, if ₹100 double itself in 10 years, is ( $\log 2 = 0.6931$ )

Solution.S:
The principal increases at a rate of $x\%$ per year, so:
$$\frac{dP}{dt} = \frac{x}{100} \times P$$

Separating the variables:
$$\frac{dP}{P} = \frac{x}{100} \, dt$$

Integrating both sides:
$$\log P = \frac{x}{100} t + c \quad \text{...... (i)}$$

When $t = 0$, $P = 100$:
$$\log 100 = c$$

When $t = 10$, $P = 200$. Substituting into (i):
$$\log 200 = \frac{x}{100} \times 10 + \log 100$$

$$\log 200 - \log 100 = \frac{x}{10}$$

$$\log 2 = \frac{x}{10}$$

$$x = 10 \log 2 = 10 \times 0.6931 = 6.931\%$$

Thus the required rate is approximately 6.93%, which corresponds to option A.
